people.paul.role: Writer in chains who prays for the Colossians
people.paul.relations: He writes with Timothy. He sends Tychicus and Onesimus to tell the readers his news.
people.paul.meaning: Paul gives thanks for the Colossians’ faith and love. He says he labors and suffers for them. He asks them to pray for him. He asks them to read this letter to the Laodiceans. He signs with his own hand and asks them to remember his chains.
people.jesus.role: Lord, image of God, and head of the assembly
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him the Son and the head of the body, the assembly. Paul says all things were created by him.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says all things were created by Jesus and through him. Paul says he is above thrones and powers. Paul says he reconciled the readers through his death. Paul then tells them to walk in him and to live as his people.
people.timothy.role: Brother named with Paul in the greeting
people.timothy.relations: The letter names him beside Paul, before it greets the Colossians.
people.timothy.meaning: Paul names Timothy as our brother in the first line. The letter says nothing else about him.
people.tychicus.role: Messenger Paul sends to tell his news
people.tychicus.relations: Paul calls him a beloved brother, faithful servant, and fellow bondservant. He goes with Onesimus.
people.tychicus.meaning: Paul says Tychicus will make all his affairs known to the Colossians. Paul sends him to learn their circumstances. He is also to comfort their hearts. Onesimus goes with him.
people.epaphras.role: Colossian who taught them and prays for them
people.epaphras.relations: Paul says Epaphras is one of them. He cares for those in Colossae, Laodicea, and Hierapolis.
people.epaphras.meaning: Paul says the Colossians learned the Good News from Epaphras. He told Paul about their love. Paul says Epaphras always strives for them in prayer. He has great zeal for them and for Laodicea and Hierapolis.
people.onesimus.relations: Paul says he is one of you, the Colossians. He goes with Tychicus.
people.onesimus.meaning: Paul calls Onesimus the faithful and beloved brother. He sends Onesimus with Tychicus. Together they will tell the Colossians everything that is going on.
places.colossae.summary: Paul writes in chapter 1 to the saints and faithful brothers at Colossae. Epaphras is one of them.
places.colossae.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.laodicea.summary: Paul struggles for the Laodiceans in chapter 2. In chapter 4 he asks that this letter be read to them. He asks the Colossians to read the letter from Laodicea. He greets Nymphas and the assembly in his house.
places.laodicea.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.hierapolis.summary: In chapter 4 Paul says Epaphras has great zeal for those in Hierapolis. He has the same zeal for Laodicea.
places.hierapolis.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: All four chapters are the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: The letter names Paul as its writer. The guide did not check authorship, date, manuscripts, or Greek forms. It did not check the prison city or the exact rival teaching. Jesus called Justus is not linked to Jesus Christ. The household commands do not show that unequal conditions ended.
sources.carlson-colossians.summary: Carlson links the readers’ new identity with changed conduct.
sources.carlson-colossians.limits: This is Carlson’s own reading. The guide did not check his Greek analysis or his links with other letters. It did not check his account of the barbarian and Scythian pair. It did not review the linked works.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-42.summary: The lesson studies changed conduct and being rooted in Christ.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-42.limits: Colossians coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters one through three. The lesson does not discuss chapter four on its own. The guide did not check the linked talks, videos, or Restoration passages.
